the_six.was: Test timeout of 90000ms exceeded, waiting for a download event
the_six.cause: NOT SLOW AND NOT A HANG - a crash the timeout was reporting late. `carriedPaintFor` decided which series survived a binding change with `next.includes(binding)`, and the panel hands over `{ ...binding, semanticKey }` - a fresh object for a binding nobody touched - so every series read as removed. The paint array emptied, `seriesPaintFor` grew it back by repeating `current.at(-1)` (undefined), and the envelope carried `palette: [null]`. `chartPaint` reads a non-record as 'must reference a palette token', so the next `snapshot()` threw `Invalid Fabric theme`; `isDirty()` runs inside React's `useSyncExternalStore`, so the throw landed in the render phase and React unmounted the whole editor. The canvas, the status line and every panel were gone, and the spec then waited 90 s for a save button that no longer existed in the document.
the_six.measurement: Repointing the starter's own sparkline from cpu.load to gpu.load unmounted the editor in 200 ms - canvas count 1 to 0, save button 1 to 0. The sparkline's settings go from `palette: [{ref: palette.frostInk}]` to `palette: [null]` across the same click. The test then passes in 10.5 s.

filed.title: The editor opens whichever theme ran last, so an author is handed a document they did not open and Save writes it over
filed.observed_live: The third run of host-player.spec.ts's chart-palette spec failed toContainText reading 'Opened E2E media' where 'Saved to library' was expected - and that fixture is seeded by global-setup itself, so bootTheme's answer to a URL naming nothing depends on which seeded theme carries the newest mtime. Status writes traced across 8 boots: the boot write lands at ~400 ms, the author's own action at ~1100 ms, so the editor is interactive ~600 ms before its own status settles. Nothing clobbered the author in 8 attempts, so it is a narrow window, not a certain failure.
filed.not_fixed: Deliberately. The one-line alternative - prefer the starter when nothing names a theme - deletes the round trip boot-theme.test.ts pins deliberately. The row asks for a decision about which store the editor assumes.

not_verified: The Playwright teardown defect did not fire in this run, so this record carries one non-firing sample rather than evidence that it is gone. The box had a second browser session on it throughout, which is the load condition that produces it.
The 200-shape acceptance probe was not re-run; it stands on plan 1's run.
No row-width measurement was taken and none is claimed. Every Chromium launch in this pass passed ignoreDefaultArgs: ["--hide-scrollbars"], and the Playwright MCP browser was never used.
